Create test sets for cross-validation

Source: R/test_sets.R
create_test_sets.Rd

Splits the locations of a dataset into training and test sets for assess_prediction(). Each test set is predicted from the rest of the data, its training set. Records at the same location are always in the same set.

Usage

create_test_sets(
  data,
  method = c("leave_one_out", "random", "cluster", "spaced"),
  n_sets = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  min_dist = NULL,
  repeats = 1,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

An sf object with point geometries, the data the models are fitted to, or a fit from glgpm().

method

How the test sets are made.

  • "leave_one_out" (the default) has one location in each test set.

  • "random" divides the locations at random into n_sets sets of about equal size.

  • "cluster" divides the locations into n_sets spatial clusters, by k-means on their coordinates.

  • "spaced" draws n_sets test sets of size locations that are at least min_dist apart.

n_sets

The number of test sets, 10 by default. With "leave_one_out" it is the number of locations, and it can't be given.

size

For "spaced" only, the number of locations in each test set.

min_dist

For "spaced" only, the smallest distance between two locations of a test set, in the units of distance of the model, which are kilometres for an sf object and distance_units for a fit.

repeats

The number of times that a "random" or "cluster" division is repeated, which gives repeats times n_sets test sets.

seed

Optional non-negative integer that makes the test sets reproducible. The caller's random number state is restored on exit.

Value

An object of class RiskMap_test_sets, a list with

sets

A list with one element for each test set, each a list of the row numbers of the training data, train, and of the test data, test.

repetition

The repeat each test set belongs to.

method

The method, or "user" for test sets given to assess_prediction() as a list.

geometry

The locations of the data, in their own CRS.

coordinates, distance_units

The projected coordinates of the rows of the data, in the units of distance.

crs

The projected CRS.

location

The distinct location of each row of the data.

min_dist, size

As given.

Details

Choose the test sets so that the test locations are about as far from their training data as the locations to be predicted are from all the data (Milà et al. 2022). plot_test_sets() with type = "distance" compares these distances. Leave-one-out and random test sets suit predictions between the locations of the data, and clusters suit predictions in areas without data. The distance min_dist of "spaced" is between the locations of a test set, which keeps them spread over the region. It isn't a distance from the training data.

Distances and clusters are computed on projected coordinates, as in glgpm(). Data in longitude and latitude are projected to the CRS that propose_crs() gives, and a fit has the CRS and the units of distance of its model.

The clusters of k-means are the best of 20 random starts. For "spaced", the locations are visited in random order and one is kept if it is at least min_dist from those kept so far, until size locations are kept or every location has been visited. A test set can therefore have fewer than size locations, and a warning says so.

Test sets made by another package

assess_prediction() also takes a list with one element for each test set, the row numbers of the test observations or a list of the training rows, train, and the test rows, test. Observations in neither are left out, for example those in a buffer around the test locations. For the folds of the rsample or the spatialsample package, this list is

lapply(folds$splits, function(split) {
  list(train = as.integer(split),
       test = as.integer(split, data = "assessment"))
})

and for folds_list of the blockCV package it is

lapply(folds$folds_list, function(fold) {
  list(train = fold[[1]], test = fold[[2]])
})

References

Milà, C., Mateu, J., Pebesma, E. & Meyer, H. (2022). Nearest neighbour distance matching Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation for map validation. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 13(6), 1304-1316. doi:10.1111/2041-210X.13851 .

See also

plot_test_sets(), which plot() of the test sets also calls, and assess_prediction(), which scores the predictions.

Examples

data(italy_sim)
example_data <- italy_sim[1:100, ]

# One location at a time
create_test_sets(example_data)
#> ── Test sets for cross-validation ──────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 10 test sets of 10 observations each from 100 observations at 10 locations.
#> Leave-one-out, with one location in each test set.
#> The distance from a test location to its nearest training location is 51.4 km
#> in the median and at most 397.9 km.
#> 
#> ℹ `plot()` maps the test sets, and `assess_prediction()` scores the predictions
#>   of models on them.

# Five spatial clusters
clusters <- create_test_sets(example_data, method = "cluster", n_sets = 5,
                             seed = 1)
clusters
#> ── Test sets for cross-validation ──────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 5 test sets of 10 to 40 observations from 100 observations at 10 locations.
#> Spatial clusters of locations, by k-means.
#> The distance from a test location to its nearest training location is 153.6 km
#> in the median and at most 397.9 km.
#> 
#> ℹ `plot()` maps the test sets, and `assess_prediction()` scores the predictions
#>   of models on them.
plot(clusters)


# Ten test sets of five locations at least 50 km apart
create_test_sets(example_data, method = "spaced", n_sets = 10, size = 5,
                 min_dist = 50, seed = 1)
#> ── Test sets for cross-validation ──────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 10 test sets of 50 observations each from 100 observations at 10 locations.
#> Locations at least 50 km apart.
#> The distance from a test location to its nearest training location is 120.2 km
#> in the median and at most 739.1 km.
#> 
#> ℹ `plot()` maps the test sets, and `assess_prediction()` scores the predictions
#>   of models on them.
